Drafting speed is no longer the bottleneck
slides.body: An LLM can generate twenty product spec summaries or tender responses in minutes. Drafting is solved.

slides.headline: Where AI generated drafts fail in industrial B2B
slides.body: Machines predict probable words. They do not understand regulatory commitments, warranties, or competitive posture.

slides.headline: Unsanctioned performance guarantees
slides.body: AI models default to superlatives. In machinery, an unverified rating becomes an expensive warranty claim.

slides.headline: Regulatory and compliance drift
slides.body: Generative tools pull global datasets. They regularly miss local statutory disclaimers or trade disclosure norms.

slides.headline: Commercial positioning erosion
slides.body: When tone is averaged across web data, your equipment sounds identical to competitors using the same models.

slides.body: Run every AI draft through this gate before sign-off.

slides.headline: Brand governance is risk management, not editing.
slides.body: Use tools to accelerate drafting. Keep senior judgement at the gate where liability lives.

caption:
AI writes copy. It cannot take risk.

Understanding what AI cannot do in brand work protects industrial marketing teams from hidden legal exposure.

The operating mistake is treating LLMs like junior writers who just need better prompts. That misses where the risk lives.

A junior writer knows when they are uncertain. An LLM outputs thermal specs, payload limits, and statutory claims with equal confidence whether accurate or invented.

When generation speeds up tenfold, the bottleneck shifts to risk review. Ungoverned speed simply generates liability faster.

Efficiency is worthless if legal withdraws your spec sheet three weeks after launch.

Send this to whoever is setting up your team's AI guidelines this quarter.
